- **Trust decision:** authorisation on UserResourceImpl's read routes decides whether a caller may read a user — the fix adds `throwIfCannotReadUserInRealm` (admin-realm + `isUserInRealm`) to `get`, `getUserClientRoles`, `getUserRealmRoles`, `getUserSessions` and `throwIfCannotAdminRealm` to `getClientRoles`, because every provider lookup underneath (`getUser(userId)`, `getUserConnections(userId)`) is realm-blind.
- **pattern_fit:** A+B — five read entry points in the published fix, one (role catalogue) with no user id, plus the READ_ADMIN-only coupled behaviour, and two untouched routes into the same identity/session decision (`disconnectUserSession`, the role-update writes).
- **Strongest lever:** reusing the existing write helper `throwIfNotSameRealm` (needs WRITE_ADMIN) or comparing `getRealmId()` to the realm name — both look right, break or half-work, and the fix's own test had to grant READ_ADMIN to prove the difference.
- **Biggest red flag:** none flagged, but the decisive caveat is that this area can only be exercised with PostgreSQL + Keycloak running (`profile/dev-testing.yml`), which is recorded in O10 and `unverified`.
